utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to call Mr. Registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is case IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor against General Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone. For the Prosecution, Sureta Chana, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, and Andres Vatter, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Henry-Benjamin. Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, representing General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Muriel Cauvin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Representing Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom, representatives of the Prosecution, both the Defence teams, the accused, the usher, the representative of the Registry, the interpreters, and all the others present in the courtroom. Today we shall continue with the cross-examination of the witness that we heard yesterday, so we are going to bring the witness into the courtroom. Usher, can you please bring the witness into the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Judge. I would like to make sure that you are receiving the interpretation. A little while ago I was told that there were technical problems. I hope that they are resolved. If you hear me, can you say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since everything is in place, I'm going to give the floor to the Defence and ask them to continue their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question to you is in relation to the legal assessment of crimes adjudicated by judges. Is it true, Mr. Adamovic, that criminal proceedings before yourself and before all other courts in our country are conducted for a crime and against a person? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the principle of the objective and subjective connexity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the legal evaluation of a crime committed by a perpetrator is given by the judge.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the final legal assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An indication as to which crime could have been committed is given first by the police, then by the prosecution, who issues an order for investigation; however, according to our law, the judge is not bound by the legal evaluation given by those bodies. A judge is independent in his qualification of the crime that was committed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the only distinction being that the criminal report submitted by the police indicates the grounds for suspicion, and this is done after certain evidence is collected. And then more evidence is collected which will corroborate the grounds for suspicion. And when this is done, then the prosecutor instigates proceedings before the court. But the judge is not bound by any of these qualifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the usher to provide the judge with the laws, because I'm going to be referring to some articles and I would like the usher to be -- to give the judge those laws so as -- for him to be able to refresh his memories when I mention some articles of these two laws.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we have been talking about so far - and that is the final qualification of a crime which is given by the Court - is determined by Article 32, 6, paragraph 2 of the Law on Criminal Procedure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you, Mr. Adamovic, to look at the Penal Code, which was taken over from the -- from the former Yugoslavia. And let's look at Article 142. The title of this article is "War crimes against the civilian population." According to our law, as you can read in the text, the person responsible for this crime is a person who either orders or commits a number of crimes which are described in paragraph 1 of this article; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is; who orders or commits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the description of the crime itself, there are certain actions such as murder, inhumane treatment, the violation of bodily integrity, unlawful incarceration, plunder, and other described actions which can be seen in the body of the text. My question to you is: Is it true, Mr. Adamovic, that these actions as separate crimes have also been envisaged by the Penal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina? For example, murder, robbery and aggravated robbery, unlawful incarceration, and so on and so forth. And although it would appear, judging from this text, that these are the same actions, we also have crimes which are envisaged by the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina which fully describes some of the actions which are described in this particular article; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The object of protection is different. In one case, if the object -- if the crime is murder, then the object of protection is human life. And in Article 142, a war crime against civilian population, the protected object is different. The civilian population is being protected from crimes committed during war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your clarification. Yesterday when you were talking about various activities of the court and other bodies of a judiciary and law-enforcement agencies, you were talking about civilian and military bodies alike. Is it true that throughout the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and especially in Zenica, the civilian bodies - that is, War Presidencies, the executive committee, the civilian protection, the civilian police - were active all this time and not for a single moment in Zenica was military administration established; and not for a moment military authorities were in control of the civilian organs?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, with the help of the usher, I would like the witness and all the other participants in the proceedings be distributed a file or a bundle which contain documents that the evidence -- that the Defence found in the archives of the cantonal court in Zenica which partially took over the cases of the district military court in Zenica; that is, those cases which are now under the jurisdiction of the cantonal court. Some of the cases in this file have already been admitted into evidence. There are three tabs here, and in front of every tab you will find the topic that is being discussed and a short description of those documents which can be found in the bundle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Adamovic, that you would regularly or on request Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of some bodies provide reports on your work? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You submitted a monthly report to the Ministry of Defence which has certain administrative authorities over the court, as you testified yesterday. At the end of the year, you would submit your report to the Supreme Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and throughout the year to all those bodies who wanted to learn about the work of the court.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is part of the regular work of the court, reporting, but not subordination. This is proper reporting as to what is being done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you please look at the document which is under tab 1, number 1. This document was produced by the district court in Zenica. The date is 12 December 1993. If we look at page 2, you will see that Muhamed Colakovic's signature is here. Was he the president of the court during that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If this is his signature, then yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information is addressed to the command of the 2nd Corps; however, I believe that this is a mistake, because you submitted such information to the 3rd Corps. I believe that this might be a typo.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be, because yesterday when we were talking about various jurisdictions and in various territories, it could have happened that the corps would cover one part of the territory over which the district military court in Zenica had jurisdiction. So this could be the case of the area being closer to Travnik and Vitez, where the jurisdictions and authorities of the two bodies overlapped. This could have been sent to the command of the 2nd Corps. It could have been sent also to the command of the 3rd Corps and to all the other units which existed in the territory of the court. The court did not change its territorial competencies, whereas the corps changed their territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, this is a new document, and we can see that this is a short analysis of the results of work for the period from the 1st to the 10th of December, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the fourth paragraph of this analysis, you can see that your court received 432 criminal cases with 860 individuals, that you finished 250 cases involving 573 individuals, and that 182 cases are pending involving 236 individuals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the following paragraph, it says that during that period you received 512 requests for investigation for 1.364 individuals, and after that followed the date on how many cases you completed. On page 2, if you look at page 2 of this document, the president of the court informs the addressee that the situation is very difficult and that the court is facing major problems with space and equipment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following paragraph speaks about what you testified about yesterday, that there was lack of paper, lack of forms, and that very often because of the lack of forms and inability to inform the witnesses and the accused, proceedings have to be delayed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document that follows. This document, on the last page again, the signature is by Muhamed Colakovic, and the date of the document is the 8th of April, 1993. It was sent to the Zenica Municipality and the executive board of the municipality, that is, the civilian body of the town of Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This report is also information on the work of the court for a shorter period. And as you can see in paragraph 2, these are reports which are drafted for the period from the 1st of October, 1993, to 25 February 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to avoid repetition, this report mentions the figures that are relative to your work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has just told me that the date of this report, as we can see, is the 8th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said October, and I confirmed that without checking the date, but that is the document we're discussing. It says "Strictly confidential, 7/94, dated the 8th of March, 1994."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in paragraph 2 of this document - in order to be quite precise and to avoid confusion, otherwise it will be of no help to the Trial Chamber - in paragraph 2 it says "According to the monthly reports sent to the Ministry of Defence, in the period from 1 October 1993 until 28 February 1994, we received 508 requests for investigations against 749 suspects." So this report deals with this brief period, as stated here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at page 3 of this report, in which you explain a fact, and before we have a look at it in the report, I'd like to ask you about this fact. In addition to the legal qualification of an act, which is the responsibility of a jurisdiction of a court, the court also independently assesses all the circumstances of importance for meting out a sentence. So the court takes into consideration aggravating or mitigating circumstances and determines the appropriate penalty, the appropriate sentence for each individual.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naturally, the prosecutor can appeal, but it is the second -- it is the appeal court that decides this.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as everywhere in the world, the judge issues a sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we have a look at this third page, you -- or rather, the court states the reasons for which certain sentences were given, and it states that "The sentences are usually either the minimum for the crimes if the accused have pleaded guilty." The court also states the reasons for this and says it's the result of assessing mitigating circumstances, personal and family circumstances, and they also talk about material conditions which were very difficult and which led to the perpetration of crimes by the accused. Is it true that these are some of the circumstances that a court had to take into consideration when deciding on the sentence?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on Criminal Procedure, there is a so-called idea of mitigating and aggravating circumstances, which has to be -- this has to be taken into consideration when determining the severity of the sentence and the type of sentence. Now when I examine the contents of this report, it is revealing in that one can understand the work of a court, in personal terms and in terms of general prevention at a time of war when the living conditions are affected by war operations. When nothing is as it usually is, certain decisions taken by the courts could have negative connotations, as far as general prevention is concerned. To prevent this from happening, the president of the court quite evidently reported regularly on how the court operated, and in this part, which is purely judicial - and it's not necessary for the court to provide anyone with reports about this, because the judge is only held accountable -- only has to report to the higher court when assessing the facts and circumstances that determine the assessment of the act or that determine the sentence - but I supported such work on the part of Mr. Colakovic, since this person is a very serious and very experienced judge, a very clever person. And knowing that prevention of a general kind could be misinterpreted by the public, he would add to his reports such elements in which he would explain why the court proceeded in a certain manner. This was more for the sake of the public, not so much for the professionals. In such exceptional circumstances, he wanted the public to be aware of why the court would deliver a certain sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adamovic, for these very precise and useful explanations. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Could we, please, now have a look at theme number 2. These are documents that talk about the court's work and about everything that you mentioned when answering questions from my colleague and myself yesterday. From 1 to 5, we have reports from on-site investigations. These are reports concerning situations in which the investigating judge would go to an on-site investigation as requested if there was information that a certain act had been committed and it was necessary to carry out an investigation in order to protect the traces of the act. The documents under 1 to 5 are new documents and they were taken from the cantonal court's archives in Zenica. Could you please have a look at the first document under number 1. This is a report on an on-site investigation which on the 26th of December, 1992 was drafted with regard to an event in which one person died. And you can see that your colleague Safet Najdin [phoen] went to the site.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your colleague Mladen Veseljak went to the site. Interpreters's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the fact that this report contains information and the facts that the judge discovered at the site, have a look at page 3. We discussed this yesterday. When present at the site, the judge undertook certain measures. Under 1, it says that he took a bullet from a military officer. He then went to the hospital to see what had happened with the person wounded. An autopsy was ordered - that's stated under 3 - he then ordered a paraffin test to be done and asked for a handgun to be seized, and he also said that someone should be put into custody for three days -- the perpetrator should be put into custody for three days to give the prosecutor time to decide whether he should continue prosecuting this case. Mr. Adamovic, these are the usual acts that a judge, in accordance with his responsibilities, does when present at an on-site investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other hand, this report, as we could see yesterday, is immediately provided to the district military prosecutor, but a copy remains in the court too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we said yesterday, and these are the copies that remain in the court, for the reasons that we mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 2, there's another report on an on-site investigation. It also concerned the death of Hasan Gafulic. You personally went to the site of this event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described what you found at the site, and then you provided detailed information on possible witnesses of that event and you stated what the witnesses told you. You then mentioned the steps taken, the measures taken. You said that the suspect was questioned. You said that was possible in exceptional circumstances. And then you ordered the military police to perform a paraffin test, but no autopsy was performed because the father of that person didn't allow you to do so. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was also provided to the district military prosecutor. The next document, under 3 - it's again another new document, as I said at the beginning, because all the documents from 1 to 5 are new documents - this is a report on an on-site investigation that your colleague, Mladen Veseljak, carried out at the site. It related to the aggravated theft and attack on military police. The situation is identical as in the previous document. Under number 4, have a look at the report on an on-site investigation dated the 23rd of July, 1993. According to this report, you went to carry out the on-site investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The situation concerned in this case had to do with accidentally firing from a weapon. The report was drafted on the 23rd of July, 1993, and you ordered the military police to take statements from people who might know something about the event. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to draw your attention - I've just remembered this - to part of my testimony yesterday. If you have a look at page 2 of this report. Have a look at the last paragraph. It says: "Given the immediate -- the vicinity of combat operations, because the scene to have crime is close to the front line, other details could not be provided, as it was necessary to act promptly." This information relates to the fact that it's important to take statements from certain individuals. I would first like to address the Judges and say that in exceptional circumstances under wartime conditions that the judges in the military court in Zenica worked in a manner that was identical to the procedure followed in peacetime. We strove when we were in -- we strove to perform our duties as professionally as possible, whenever this was possible, and with regard to the testimony about the professionalism of people in wartime, you will make your own assessment, but my claim was that whenever the judge was called on to perform its duty, it did so professionally. This report, dated the 23rd of July, 1993 was drafted at the time of combat, as there was fighting which was ongoing and we attempted to obtain evidence that someone had been accidentally killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the next page, you can see that you provided these documents to OVP Zenica. That means the district military prosecutor's office in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And VP, which means the military police battalion. It wasn't our duty to provide this to the military police battalion, but the court always attempted to provide everyone with information in case something got lost because of the exceptional circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this particular case, this is what you did, because on page 2 it says that you gave the military police certain tasks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We provided this for the sake of information, so we wanted to have a full circle, the possibility of finding documents in certain archives at all times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, could we have a look at the document under number 5 now. The title of the document is not a report on an on-site investigation, but the title is "An official record." The judge went to the area of the municipality of Vares, though. The judge who went there -- in fact, there were two judges, Armin Zeco and Mladen Veseljak, your colleagues from the district military court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the description of the site, it's possible to see that on the 20th of August, 1993 - that was the date of this -- that's the date of this report - the bodies of some individuals were taken to the village of Dragovici. The traces had been destroyed. The site had been tampered with. And at the site itself it was -- there was a perpetual danger because of sniper activity, so that these judges could not go to carry out an on-site investigation. That's what it says under number 1, "Description of the crime scene"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this case, it involves the death of four Bosniaks. We don't know what the cause of death was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the information on the victims states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3 it also says that the judge took certain measures, the body was examined externally, and then Dr. Faruk Turkic, a pathologist, compiled an external description of the body and that was an integral part of the record. When the court couldn't go to the site because of combat, was this something that could be done? And such reports would again be provided to the military prosecutor; or rather, they could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. provide such reports to the military police as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first page, where it says "those present," it says that Zeco, with Judge Veseljak, went on behalf of the military court. This was done when it was essential to carry out many -- to take many steps. In such a case, one judge would help another judge to expedite the procedure. But to the right you can see under "Others" that Mr. Hasagic is mentioned as the high judge. Mr. Mutapcic is mentioned as the deputy public prosecutor. So I can draw the conclusion that when information was received on the case in fact nothing more was known; all that was known was that the bodies were found in the immediate vicinity of the front line, and it seems that the crime was perpetrated against these individuals but we don't know whether member of the army or some civilian committed this act. And when I said that there was full cooperation, when the people involved were normal, this is such a case. Both civilians -- or rather, representatives of civilian court went to the site and representatives of the military court, which was also a civilian court but dealt with people in uniform, and they would decide what action to take on the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We have just had a look at a selection of reports on on-site investigations, but would it be correct to say that after such investigations and after the documents had been provided to the military prosecutor the procedure that was then followed and the action taken by other organs was only done when requested by the authorised military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if these steps were taken. So it was always problematic for us - and I've repeated this on many occasions - it was always a problem for us to know what was happening. If we were aware of what had happened and if we received information, this was the procedure that was followed. And the prosecutor would then take certain steps; he would contact the judge. And I wanted people's professionalism to be compared in peacetime and wartime, but you will see that the procedure followed was the same procedure that was followed in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's briefly look at the documents between 16 and 14 [as interpreted], not to see what it says in them but just for me to ask you several questions about the facts as to which body submitted reports -- criminal reports to the military prosecution, when this was done, and how this was described. And all these criminal reports that are in the bundle are new documents. The Defence found them in the cantonal court in Zenica during their investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'm going to try and help the interpreters. I'm going to make a pause between the answer and the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, can we just briefly look at the documents. The first document is the criminal report by the military police which was submitted on the 4th of December, 1992. And the event in question, as we can see in the explanation, is the event that happened on the 29th of October, 1992. The police described the event, and the police qualified this as robbery as described in Article 150 in the penal law of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second criminal report was also addressed to the prosecutor, military prosecutor. It was filed by the military police of one of the brigades. There is a short description of the crime. And here again the police qualified this as robbery. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 148, paragraph 3, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second part, this is Mirsad Jasarevic, and this was qualified as robbery as per Article 150 of the Penal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So this would be a crime of robbery.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After number 8, there is also another criminal report filed by the battalion of the military police dated -- against Latif Delic. The date is 10 June 1993, the crime was committed in May 1993. The police qualified this incident as an aggravated robbery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Actually, there was some property taken from an abandoned house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following document is a criminal report issued by the 355 Brigade, and the date is August 1993. Again, the police qualified the incident as illegal trade. Is that correct? You can look at other criminal reports. Some of them were filed by the civilian police, the Security Services Centre, that is.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about that yesterday. Both the civilian police and the military police had equal say in filing criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues are warning me that there is no answer to one of my questions, that the answer has not been recorded to my question about a criminal report which was filed in August 1993. The police qualified this incident as an illegal trade. My questions was: "Is that correct?" But the answer was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have mentioned a lot of things. I don't know what you were referring to. What criminal report did you refer to in your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see. This is number 9, the 1st of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 129, illicit trade. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Having had a look at all of these criminal reports, would you say that they confirm that the military prosecutor would receive reports mostly from the military bodies, the battalion of the military police or other military bodies, but that there were also cases when the military prosecutor's office also received reports from the civilian police or the CSB? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There were reports by the military police, the brigade commands, the civilian police. You also file some reports -- find some reports filed by citizens. Everybody who wanted to do so or who had had an occasion to do so could file those criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look at documents from number 15 to number 17. Again, these are new documents that the Defence was able to locate in the archives of the cantonal court in Zenica, which has taken over some of the cases of the military district court in Zenica. Yesterday you were talking about a situation in which there was evidence with the criminal report or the evidence that you as judges submitted to the prosecution from your on-site investigation, and if this evidence was enough to instigate an indictment - and we're talking about crimes for which the punishment envisaged was up to ten years - then the prosecutor could instigate the proceedings without any further investigation. Can you please look at these three documents and confirm that this illustrates what you were talking about yesterday and that this illustrates the legal procedure and the legal -- pertinent legal text. We're talking about 15, 16, and 17, documents numbered 15, 16, and 17.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the so-called shortened proceedings, and a possibility for an immediate address to the court, addressing the court immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all of these three cases, the prosecutor gives its prior qualification of the crime and gives a detailed description of the crime. And it is only this description that the judge is bound by when giving the final qualification of a crime.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at documents from 18 to 20. Number 18 is a document dated 16 February 1993, and 20 is 27 July 1993. And in the first case, this means that the document dated 16 February 1993, this is a decision ordering detention against a person. You, as the investigating judge, issued that order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And from the Statement of Reasons, in paragraph 3 you can see the reasons for which this was done, mentioning the seriousness of the crime, the consequences of the crime, the need to carry out an investigation. And there's also an indication that the suspect might flee, and this is one of the reasons why detention was ordered against this person. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Why am I saying this? Because even during the war conditions, there was still a need to explain things. And if we were to compare this with the Geneva Convention on fair trial, we could see that there was a lot of comparison to be done between what we did and what is prescribed by the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were talking about it yesterday, and I am showing this document to you to ask you whether this decision was issued after an on-site investigation. There was still no request for investigation. But if you look at the document under number 19, the official record, you will see that the prosecutor, who is the only person in charge for ordering detention, that he did do that, and this was your grounds for issuing this decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now can we look at documents number 21 to 30. We are going to see how the court worked and how the prosecutor's office worked. These documents show that the prosecutors are the ones who provide the judge and the court with the request for an investigation, and this is followed by the court's decision on the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, all of these documents are new documents, which were found in the cantonal court in Zenica during the investigation carried out by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first document bears the date 6 October 1993. It was sent to the district military court, to the investigating judge there. And the request was submitted to the investigating judge for an investigation to be carried out against two persons who have committed certain crimes, which are described in this request and which the prosecutor qualified as the robbery of arms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document under number 22 is a similar request for an investigation to be carried out. The date is 14 October 1993. Again, it is requested from the investigating judge to carry out an investigation for the crimes which took place in July 1993, when the abandoned houses were looted, the abandoned Croatian houses were looted. And if we look at page 2, the penultimate paragraph which begins with the title "I propose," it is clear that this request was issued based on the criminal reports of the Municipal Staff of Vares, dated 11 August 1993. In other words, we may agree that it did take some time for the prosecutor to verify the allegations, and it was only one or two months later that he issued a request for an investigation to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that this was the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following document is also a request for an investigation which was submitted on the 15th of November, 1993, and the event took place on the 12th of November, 1993, which means that the military police was very efficient in locating and arresting the persons who perpetrated the crime. In this particular case, the investigating judge was able to act already on the following day.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is the civilian part, the regular court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, since we were talking about the procedure and the procedure being practically identical?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is also proof, isn't it, that the person under number 1, a member of the BiH army, that the other persons were not members of the BiH army and that in keeping with Article 9 of the law on military district courts, in such a situation the jurisdiction for the prosecution of both military persons and the civilians lies in the hands of the civilian judges and the civilian prosecutor's offices; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would not propose to go through all of these documents, but based on such requests, can you please look at document number 24. This is a decision to open an investigation. The date is 4th of December, 1992. This was issued by the investigating judge based on the request of the military prosecutor and this decision serves to open an investigation and that during this investigation all the actions proposed by the prosecution will be carried out, and also the actions that the accused and his Defence counsel suggest during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, the document under number 25, which is another decision of the investigating judge to open an investigation. The qualification of this crime was murder. This is a decision issued on the 7th of January, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document bearing the date of the 16th of August, 1993 is absolutely identical. Here the person is accused of having committed an aggravated robbery stemming from Article 148 of the Penal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina. These document, that is, a decision to open an investigation by the investigating judges, is actually the first judiciary qualification of the crime, and the final qualification is issued by the presiding judge or the presiding -- or the panel of judges.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document under number 30. This is a ruling issued by yourself by which the already ongoing investigation is terminated or suspended. Once the judge suspends the investigation, the prosecution may deem that there's not enough evidence, and he may want to suspend the investigation. In this particular case --

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we looking at number 30?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, number 30, and the date on the document is 25 December 1993.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you are not right in your explanation. Here the investigation was suspended for a different reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'll come to that. But the general principle is as follows: When the prosecutor informs the investigating judge that there are no further grounds for prosecution, then the proceedings are suspended.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? May I answer your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here this is about the right of the judge to suspend the proceedings. There is such a right. And this right is initiated either on the request of the parties or ex officio. In this particular case, 87/93 dated 25 December 1993, this is not an investigation but the trial. In deciding on the prosecution's request, the judge established that the person against whom the criminal proceedings were instigated died, and that was the reason why the proceedings were terminated. This is one of the rights and obligations of the court, to terminate proceedings against a deceased. However, irrespective of that, of the document that you are showing me, however, in relation to what you have been saying, you're absolutely right; a judge may terminate any proceedings under certain circumstances and under certain conditions. This is the right of every judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I was a little fast, but you have now clarified everything. The judge's right is to suspend the investigation when the prosecutor abandons the case or if there are other conditions. And secondly, when in the course of the proceedings it is established that the accused has died, because if the prosecutor had decided not to prosecute and the accused was alive, you wouldn't have suspended the proceedings; you would have declared the indictment null and void; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the difference I was pointing to, because a sentence is how a trial is put to an end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at documents from 31 to 34 now. These are documents from the 27th of November, 1993, the 20th of December, 1993, a document dated the 14th of September, 1994. Those are the documents. Yesterday when explaining how the courts worked, you said that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after the investigation had been completed, the prosecutor, who was the main person in the proceedings, would decide whether the proceedings should be suspended, because there was no evidence, or whether an indictment would be issued. These are examples of indictments that the court was provided with the military prosecutor after the investigation had been completed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first case, we can see that the prosecutor accused two persons for an event on the 29th of October, 1992. The indictment was issued on the 27th of November, 1993. This means that to detect the event and investigate it lasted for almost one year, after which the prosecutor collected sufficient evidence to accuse these individuals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly - and this is what we can see from the document - the Prosecutor previously described these acts a -- on the basis of Article 160 of the adopted ZKP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he qualified them as burglary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is an item -- is an indictment that was issued on the 27th of December, 1993. It was addressed to the district military court. It had to do with an event on the 26th of August, 1993 and it related to the previous legal qualification provided by the prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is also an indictment from the military court. These indictments were just taken as examples of the kind of work you described before the Chamber yesterday. You recognise this indictment as an indictment issued by the district military court in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now have a look at the documents from 34 to 53, but by mistake we have a number 36 in the list, whereas we have no such document. We just skipped a number. When you have a look, you will see that these documents are judgements from the district military court in Zenica. And I will only refer to a number of these judgements. Just have a look at them and tell us whether you recognise these as judgements of the district military court. And they perhaps are from the regular court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the whole, these are judgements from the district military court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we have a look at the first judgement under number 34 in the list. We can see that it's a judgement dated the 3rd of April, 1993, issued by the Chamber of the district military court, and you were its president; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the introduction in the preamble, we can see that the proceedings were on the basis of the indictment KT328/92, dated the 2nd of February, 1993, and we can conclude that the court proceeded very quickly in this case because a judgement was taken two months later, on the 3rd of April, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The description of the act shows that the event itself took place on the 13th of December, 1992. This period, from December 1992 up until the 2nd of February, 1993, was the period during which the investigation was conducted. So one could say that the investigation was completed quite rapidly in this case too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2, at the bottom it says "by which they committed," and then you have under number 1 "the accused Jasmin Vikovic." These acts described above were described by you as violent behaviour, as the crime of damaging property and the crime of aggravated theft; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we have a look at page 3, you gave all of these individuals a certain prison sentence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were given single prison sentences in the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is also a judgement from your court, dated the 14th of May, 1993. It has to do with an event that took place on the 6th of December, 1992, and your colleague, Muhamed Colakovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President, excuse me, please. Mr. President, the face of the documents speak for themselves, and I really don't want to assist my friend in her case, but the Prosecution has no objections at all if she were to just put in the documents, because all the judgements are basically the same, and I don't think it's necessary for us to go through each and every document, because they will speak for themselves from their face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You could perhaps save time, unless certain documents concern substantial issues and you would like the witness to comment on them. Otherwise, you could speed up, because there is no objection to these very official documents from a military court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, you've heard my colleague's very reasonable suggestion. I think that we could have you have a look at the documents and you could then confirm that these are judgements from the district military court. I think that that is the case for all the documents, apart from one of them. Could you just confirm this. Could we have a look at the judgement under number 45.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These really are judgements from the district military court in Zenica, which can be seen from the names of the judges, whom I know, and the description of the procedure followed in the military court. I have to tell you of the feelings I have when I see these documents, when I see the dates and the judgements consisting of tens of scores of pages. It really shows how much attention we paid to these matters. One should not forget that there was a war going on and we undertook these activities very professionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is important for the Judges to understand. Have a look at the judgement under number 45, dated the 11th of July, 1995. Have you found the judgement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 264/94. You were a judge in this case, and you found a certain individual guilty for -- because on the 12th of June, 1993 in the village of Kakanj this individual seized some property from Croats, and you described this act as the crime of theft; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also took a cow, seized a cow.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This judgement also shows that the event that took place on the 12th of June, 1993 was an event for which the individual was accused in the indictment KT406/94, the 6th of May, 1994. He was only judged on the 11th of July, 1995, which shows that the court, when collecting evidence and conducting its work, encountered many obstacles, many problems. And this has already been mentioned in relation to your predecessor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the basis of the contents of this document, you can see that the prosecution case arrived on the 6th of May, 1995, and the judgement was on the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The date was the 6th of May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was perhaps not possible to gain access to Sikira, but there wasn't an investigation carried out. The prosecutor directly contacted the court. So the event was in 1993, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in mid-1993 -- it took place in mid-1993, and the prosecutor contacted the court in mid-1994. My conclusion would be that the prosecutor held onto the case for about a year, probably because this individual was not available and the court, in fact, when searching for this individual, found it difficult to find him. The case in itself was not a problematic one. That's quite obvious. But if it's a driver - and that's what it says in the information provided - then it is obvious that this is a person who moved around a lot, and we could not gain access to him, if he was a member of the army. So a simple case such as this one was probably difficult for these reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at a similar case. It's under number 46, your colleague Veseljak dealt with it. It's a judgement dated the 15th of August, 1995. One person was accused on the basis of the indictment in this case, so an investigation was conducted. The event took place in July 1993. It was a matter of stealing money from Croats. The judge described this crime as the crime of theft, and the judgement was issued on the 15th of August, 1995. So if we accept your explanation that you provided a minute ago, even in the case of simple crimes, quite a lot of time could pass before a judgement was issued because there were various circumstances which made it impossible for courts to summon the accused, to summon witnesses, et cetera. So is this more proof that there were such situations in wartime conditions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to what we discussed previously and in relation to this case, I attempted to deal with this in various manners. It was always important for us for events to be discovered and to be reported as soon as possible, and once it entered the judicial procedure, then it would be dealt with in a year, in two years, or in three years. The important thing was not to forget the case; it was important for it not to be concealed and it was important to process it in a regular manner. This case shows that there were problems when accusing someone and when putting someone on trial, and this was -- these problems occurred for various reasons. But the important thing was to have this crime reported, to have the crime processed, and to have the person judged. If you have a look at the judgements and the previous judgements, we wanted to ensure that the army did not consider war booty to be something that was quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a look at -- at the documents under tab 3. It has to do with Susanj. As the investigating judge, would it be correct to say that you were informed that a certain number of bodies were taken to the hospital -- to the morgue of the hospital in the area of Susanj? It's under tab 3. We have some documents under that tab, from 1 to 15. Documents from 1 to 6 have already been admitted into evidence, whereas the other ones are new documents, and they're -- they haven't been -- they were taken from the archives of the cantonal court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you were saying a minute ago, when you asked me whether I was aware of the fact that a certain number of bodies had been taken to the morgue of the hospital in Zenica, well, that sounded like a quote, because that's something that I used in an official report, under number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date is the 12th of June, 1993. The prosecution number is 03403591.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to discuss all of the events. You were informed, and together with your colleague Hidajet Halilhodzic you went to the morgue to establish the facts of the matter.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was also Muris Hadziselimovic, the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your colleague Hidajet Halilhodzic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Hidajet, but this should be found here. I don't think he was there, but if that is what it says, then he was, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have already discussed about this event. Before this Trial Chamber, I would kindly ask you to look at the documents. The first document is the one sent by the chief of security of the 3rd Corps. The date is 10 June 1993, and this is document number 1. In this document, it says that the military police was present during the identification of the bodies that had been brought to the morgue. The military police went to the site of the event, and the persons who were identified are mentioned. I don't know whether you're familiar with this document. Have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's under number 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very easy for you to say, but I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 3, numbered 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my bundle, it's not so easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a big number 3, and after this you will find a theme "Susanj," and then number 1, and under number 1 you will find it, I'm sure. While you are looking--

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have two more questions that I would like to put to the witness, and my colleague Ibrisimovic told me that he would only need 15 minutes. I would need 10 more minutes, and if you will allow me, I would like to use the 15 minutes that my colleague Ibrisimovic is not going to use, and I'm going to use that time to put my questions to the witness and then my colleague Ibrisimovic will only need 15 minutes. If you will allow me to proceed in this way. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can somebody assist me with finding this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, this is a list showing all the documents and if you turn to number 1, this will be the report issued by the security body of the 3rd Corps. My question to you is whether you have ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to this here, this is totally illegible. That's why I skipped it. I don't know what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at number 2. The previous document has already been admitted into evidence as DH258. Under number 2, you can see the cover of a file, KRI 162/93. This is a corps document and this is a typical marking of the document that contains the record on an on-site investigation, the official records by the judges, and so on and so forth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first document speaks about the request issued by the higher public prosecutor sent to Dr. Faruk Turkic, pathologist, to provide the prosecutor's office with information as to whether a postmortem had been carried out. The second document you can find here was a document that was sent to you. Actually, it was you who sent this document to the deputy public prosecutor, Suada Halilagic, following her request, which is the third document under this tab. On the 5th of October, 1993 the deputy prosecutor, Suada Halilagic, requested some additional information from you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correspondence between the civilian courts, the military court, because it was not known at the time who would be in charge of the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following document is a confirmation that you issued to the father of one of the deceased. The date of the document is 16 July 1993, and you issued this document in order to enable the father to bury the body of his son.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was very important whether the body was in a uniform or not because of the different entitlements which stemmed from that fact. And here it says that the person was who he was and a short description.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following four documents. These are the delivery notes by way of which you deliver the official records that you yourself had compiled. You deliver that note to various bodies. And for the record, the whole set of the records has already been admitted as DH61. At the end, you can find your report to the executive committee of the Zenica Municipality. They were also interested in what had happened, and you provide them with short information on what you had found out.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a very unusual incident, and everybody was very interested in what happened. And as far as I was concerned, I wanted to inform all the relevant bodies, the law enforcement bodies, and the military bodies. I informed them that the number of bodies in civilian clothes was too big to be justified by war operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following document is the official record that we are talking about. This is what you compiled on the 12th of June. Is it correct that the first part of this record, in which you state and describe injuries found on 14 bodies as well as the situation with bodies brought over under 16, 17, and 18, this was all done in the presence of pathologist Turkic and a representative of the military prosecutor's office? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reminder of the official record was compiled by you yourself on your own, once you had received information from the representatives of the civilian protection, Ilijas Tatarovic, who had informed you that some of the bodies had been buried in the territory of Cukle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those bodies were identified, and so on and so forth. Yes, this can be found on the last page. Nothing was done here. This is just information that I received from Ilijas Tatarovic, the representative of the civilian protection, just to set up a trail as to what bodies had been buried for the reasons of a possible subsequent quest [as interpreted]. This is just information that will serve to help locate those bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 4 of the official record, Mr. Adamovic, you stated that you wanted to go to the site but that the military police -- actually, the army that you found on the spot, you had learnt that it wouldn't be safe for you to go to the site and that's why you didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second reason was that the bodies had already been moved, that the traces of the incident had been destroyed; and the third reason was that your possible visit to the site would not facilitate the investigation. These are your conclusions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct. I was prevented by the army from going to the site. They didn't allow me to go there. Now, why have I always emphasised the way the court worked? Every time we received information, we wanted to carry out our investigation in the most professional way possible. In this particular event -- I remember this event very well because of the huge number of bodies that were involved, especially because it involved a family of one of our former colleagues, a judge, and these are the details that stick in my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have recorded all that in your official record.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Allow me. So because of the way we worked and because of all the other details that I have just mentioned, the number of bodies, and because of the fact that this involved the relatives of a colleague of mine with whom I used to work, I wanted at any cost to go to the site. We came there. I had police escort. We arrived in two or three vehicles and the soldiers stopped us and told us that it would not be safe for us to go up there. I told them that I would go there irrespective of the fact that it might not be safe. And then one of my escorts explained to the soldier that I was a judge and that I had the right to go wherever I wanted to go, because this soldier denied me the right to go to the site. Then I asked him to inform his command in order to resolve the situation. And after that, I was banned from accessing the area, from going there. And that is why I had to compile such a long official record. On my return, I had to make a note of having been prevented from going there. I don't know what happened, whether the soldier abused his position or whether he had received his orders from the command. I don't know, to this very day. However, I recorded what had happened. Against my will I was banned from going to the site. I did want to go there, and I had to record that. There was another record which shows that we even went to the trenches, where we were within the axis of the enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have already seen two situations: One in which you couldn't complete your investigation due to war operation; and the second, where your colleague, Veseljak, also couldn't do that. However, all that happened you recorded in your official note. And this is your official note, your official record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is not identical to what I was talking about yesterday. This is a case of me having been prevented from going to the site, and I was not very happy with that. I was very unhappy, actual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, Mr. Adamovic, please look at document number 4, this is Defence Exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are being warned, Mr. President, that the time has come for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is unfortunate that we have to make a break, but we have to for technical reasons, so we shall make a break until 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall resume, and I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, kindly look at document number 5. A little while ago, when I showed you document 3, we saw the correspondence between yourself and the deputy public prosecutor, Mrs. Suada Halilagic, in which you informed her that a submission had been set up that, the president of that commission was Jusuf Halilagic, and that you had compiled a report signed by yourselves. Can you please look at this report. Is this the report that you, as a member of this commission set up pursuant to the order of the 3rd Corps Command and at the request of the deputy commander of the Command Staff, compiled?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was due to the fact that the situation was exceptional, and I as a judge found myself in that exceptional situation. My escorts had wanted to shoot at the troops in order to secure my passage. I found that completely insane, and I suspended all my further attempts to go to the site. However, through these reports, I informed all the relevant bodies of what had happened. And one day I was invited to attend a meeting. At that meeting, there were these gentlemen present. I was told at that meeting that the information on what had happened was indeed received, that measures would be taken in that respect. I signed that. I was sure that all the information had been forwarded, and this is what it says in this report. So this is my participation in the entire event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the letter that we saw a little while ago that you sent to your colleague Halilagic, you actually pointed to this report and you stated that Mr. Halilagic from the 3rd Corps, who was the president of that commission, compiled a special report on the order of the deputy commander, Mr. Siber Stjepan. At the moment when you were providing answer to my question, you did not have that document before you, but now you have it, and you recognised your signature on the report that had been compiled.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are we talking about now? We were talking about this report or what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that, we saw this document KRI.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the number of that, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number is 2 in the bundle of documents, and the first document after this report is a request for the pathologist, Dr. Turkic, and the second document is your response to your colleague, Suada Halilagic, the one that you have just recognised.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the significance of this situation and the fact that a judge had been prevented from carrying out an on-site inspection, this was my next step, in order to be sure that the information to my superiors would indeed be forwarded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Adamovic, as of this moment, since all the information - that is, your official note, the official note compiled by the military police, the photos, and the report of the commission - were in the hands of the prosecutor, it was up to the prosecutor to manage the proceedings and issue orders to the competent bodies as to what needs to be done next.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you to look at the documents from 7 to 15, documents that you probably have not seen before, but they will serve for my following questions: Is this now a customary procedure according to which, if you look at these documents from 7 to 15, for which I'm sure that you have not seen them before, but my question to you is as follows: Is this now a customary procedure and the way the prosecutor acts in his quest for additional information? So the prosecutor is the one who checks all the existing information in order to establish whether the crimes had indeed been committed and who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we said earlier on that information was forwarded specifying who had to perform certain duties, well, the report shows that the judge was prevented from carrying out the on-site investigation. The army should have investigated why this happened, because that is also a crime, in a certain sense, and they should have reported this to the prosecutor's office that had jurisdiction, and independently of the reasons for which the judge went there. It could have been a matter of abuse, and they should have -- and as far as whether somebody was done within the army in that respect, I know nothing about this, but the district military prosecutor had information on the grounds for suspicion for crimes that were determined on the basis of what the civilian bodies had discovered. According to what you have shown me, it seems that the civilian prosecutor took steps as is customary for a prosecutor, but I would rather see what the military prosecutor did in this respect. But no error was made because the civilian prosecutor on the grounds for suspicion also was in a position to take those steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But let me finish. However, from the very beginning, it was quite clearly indicated that those bodies had been brought in from a zone of combat and so one would expect that the military prosecutor or the security organs in the corps in question would be the first to take these steps. It would be their responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. I have a few more questions regarding a subject that you discussed with my learned colleague from the Prosecution, and this has to do with the fact that from a large number of citizens you found out that members of their family were taken away and they told you that they suspected that they had been taken to the music school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as this information from the citizens is concerned, you didn't file a criminal report or make an official record. You referred those people to the military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military prosecutor's office and the military court were in the same building but on different floors. The court was on an upper floor and the prosecution was below. So a party would pass by the prosecutor's office when going to the court. It was very easy for us to send the citizen downstairs to see the prosecutor. But the court and the prosecutor's office were aware of the fact that people would arrive. Whether the prosecutor made a report of this or not, I don't know if that was his duty, but this situation was very familiar, so we didn't make a record of this. Sometimes - and I think that this is something you can find in the court archives - on certain occasions someone would make certain records, if a particular detail was emphasised or someone's identity was mentioned, if someone had recognised someone. Then a record of this would be made in the court too, and this was usually done if the information arrived in the afternoon, if there was only an on-duty judge. If someone was waiting in front of the court and the judge was required to come, this would be done. In the course of our working hours, this is a matter we would refer to the prosecutor, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw these citizens and referred them to the prosecutor's office, the prosecutor, on the basis of the law, had the duty of making a record or of telling the citizens how to file a report on the event.

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prosecutor has to see all the citizens and take into consideration all reports. Organs have to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you just said, if the prosecution accepts or receives a report, it is their duty to act on the report and to refer to certain organs to check these matters, or on the basis of these reports it is the prosecutor's duty to engage in prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that on one occasion you went to the music school under the escort of European monitors. You were in the basement while they were visiting the building. You said that you didn't see anyone there but that you subsequently found out that one person that they were searching for had been concealed in the attic. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information according to which the European monitors also visited the music school on other occasions and that they didn't find anyone in detention there? Did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they had such authority. As to whether they entered the building or not, I don't know. That was part of their work, and they didn't inform me of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Adamovic, would it be correct to say that this fact, the fact that you discovered that someone had been concealed, might indicate that some people in the music school were involved in fairly illegal acts which they concealed from any organs that might want to investigate the situation to determine what the actual situation in the music school was?
