utterances.text: Yes, it had been agreed between the army and the civilian authorities that the army would move on and that the civilian protection would clean up the terrain. What they forgot to mention is that they had forgotten to call a judge or a prosecutor or the police in order for them to see whether there is any proof of violent deaths which had nothing to do with the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My next question is relative to a question put to you by Honourable Judge Swart. He asked you about these documents relative to the identification of the bodies in January. Our investigators have inspected the archives of the cantonal court. I can confirm to you, although that may not be relevant, that all of these documents can be found in the cantonal court in Zenica. My question to you is as follows: Is it true that it was not only the wish of the judge to forward all the documents to the prosecutor but that this is an obligation provided for in Article 150 according to which anything received by the judge which points to a crime, the judge cannot retain such a document but has to forward it to the prosecutor immediately for the prosecutor to institute proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 150 talks about the criminal report, but it may also be the case that the judge receives something that is not relevant at all. In that case, a judge will employ his common reasoning and see what to do with such papers. Generally speaking, the judges will forward everything to the prosecutors because the prosecutors are in charge of prosecution, at the same time retaining copies of all the documents. The judges are not the ones who will evaluate documents. It will be the prosecutor who will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, after everything is submitted to the prosecutor, the dominus litus - that is, the master of further proceedings in the criminal procedure - is the prosecutor and all the others will act on his request or on his order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO ADAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the prosecution. However, if human rights are violated, then a request has to be put to the judge for any further proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The other Defence team, do they have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, we don't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Benjamin, do you have any additional question for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a moment I was afraid that you would have to spend the weekend in The Hague; however, owing to the expediency of all the parties, this will not be the case. We would like to wish you a happy journey back home, and we wish you a lot of success in your future career as a judge. I'm going to ask Mr. Usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Benjamin, next week's schedule. You have the floor. Inform us, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm happy to inform the Court that we have a full list scheduled for next week. Monday, the 28th of June is the internal witness, investigator Peter Hackshaw. On Tuesday, the 29th, this witness was earlier scheduled to be a videolink witness, but I'm happy to inform the Court that he has now recovered fully and will be -- he'll be here live. That's Vinko Zrno. On Wednesday, the 30th of June, this is one of the witnesses that Mr. Mundis has just completed proofing and that's one of the 3rd Corps people with the orders. Thursday, the 1st of July, we expect to have the witness -- the other videolink witness, and I'm yet to receive further information on that because of the nature of the witness I cannot communicate with him directly. And on Friday, we have the second witness with respect to the insider, so to speak, Muradit Mekic, and that takes care of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that all the witnesses who were scheduled will be heard next week. We are approaching the 1st of July, the end of the Prosecution case; am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes and no. Yes, in the sense that all witnesses will be finished with. But I think the Chamber had alerted the Prosecution that there was some tidying up to do with documents and so we couldn't really close before that was done. Mr. Mundis, who is more familiar with that aspect, will be here on Monday and he'll be able to give the Court further guidance and say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As far as the Defence is concerned, we still have a couple of minutes. Are there any points you wish to raise at this moment? There is nothing. Mrs. Benjamin, is there anything you wish to raise at this point?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will therefore adjourn until Monday at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of June, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
